## What This Is

This folder contains **architecture guidance** for the Endpoint Security domain. All content is aligned to TOGAF ADM Phases A–D and the Architecture Content Framework. Documents here define *what* the Endpoint Security architecture must achieve and *how* it should be structured — not *how* to configure specific tools or *what* controls to implement.

<!-- AI-GENERATED-START | user:mygainwell | date:2026-10-22 | model:GitHub Copilot -->
> **Enterprise parent:** Endpoint Security guidance elaborates the [Enterprise Security Architecture Vision](../GUID-SEC-ARCHITECTURE-VISION-0.0.01.md). The Endpoint Security vision remains the immediate parent for this domain's capability, ABB, and RAD documents.
<!-- AI-GENERATED-END | user:mygainwell | date:2026-10-22 -->
page_texts.3:
[strategy/guidance/security/Endpoint/README.md#what-this-is-not]

## What This Is NOT

- **Not security standards or controls**: Configuration baselines, NIST SP 800-53 control implementations, and audit requirements belong in `standards/security/`. Nothing in this folder is enforceable as a security standard.
- **Not Solution Building Blocks**: Vendor product selection, implementation runbooks, and platform-specific configuration are Phase E–F outputs and are not documented here.
- **Not an architecture decision record**: Significant architectural decisions are recorded in `decisions/security/`.

[strategy/guidance/security/Endpoint/README.md#content-types]

## Content Types

| Type | What It Is | TOGAF Phase |
|---|---|---|
| **Architecture Vision** | Establishes why the Endpoint Security architecture exists, its strategic scope, and the success criteria that authorize all ABBs | Phase A |
| **Capability Map** | L1/L2 capability model — the structured, non-ABB description of what the Endpoint Security domain does | Phase B |
| **Capability Descriptions** | Narrative elaboration of each L2 capability — what it does, why it matters, who depends on it | Phase A–B |
| **Composite ABB** | The parent Architecture Building Block defining the full Endpoint Security architectural hierarchy | Phase B–D |
| **ABB Alignment Matrix** | Traceability catalog mapping every ABB to its L2 capability, status, and paired Reference Architecture | Phase B–D |
| **Component ABBs** | Individual reusable ABBs for each Endpoint Security capability area — solution- and vendor-agnostic | Phase B–D |
| **Reference Architectures** | Illustrative, non-prescriptive patterns showing how ABBs compose into deployment-ready architectures | Phase C–D |

## Reading Order

> Start with the Vision. Read capability modeling documents before ABBs. Read ABBs before Reference Architectures.

```
1. GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-VISION-0.4.01.md          Architecture Vision (Phase A) — start here
2. GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-CAP-MAP-0.4.02.md         Capability Map L1/L2 (Phase B)
3. GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-CAP-DESC-0.4.03.md        Capability Descriptions (Phase A–B)
4. GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-COMPOSITE-1.4.02.md       Composite ABB (Phase B–D)
5. GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-ABB-MATRIX-2.4.11.md      ABB Alignment Matrix (Phase B–D)
6. [Component ABBs below]                       Component ABBs (Phase B–D)
7. ref-arch/[Reference Architectures]           Reference Architectures (Phase C–D)
```

## Adjacent Domain Boundaries

| Domain | Boundary Description | Primary Interface Document |
|---|---|---|
| **Identity Security** | Device posture signals (from this domain) combine with user identity trust signals (from IAM domain) at the Zero Trust PDP for access decisions | [GUID-SEC-IAM-REF-2.2.01](../Identity/GUID-SEC-IAM-REF-2.2.01.md) |
| **Security Operations** | Endpoint telemetry and EDR alerts flow to SecOps for correlation, detection, and response | GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-TELEM-2.4.10, GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-EDR-2.4.04 |
| **Network Security** | Device managed-status and posture compliance informs network access control | GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-DEVICE-TRUST-2.4.07 |
| **Information Security** | Data classification policies drive endpoint DLP enforcement | GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-EDP-2.4.09 |
